Surah 35 (Fatir) — Makkan

{1} He (Allah, exalted is He) praises His noble and sanctified Self for creating the heavens and the earth and what they contain of creatures, because that is evidence of the perfection of His power, the vastness of His dominion, the comprehensiveness of His mercy, the wondrous nature of His wisdom, and the encompassing of His knowledge. Having mentioned creation, He then mentioned what involves command, namely that He made {the angels messengers}: in executing His decreed commands (al-qadariyyah), and as intermediaries between Him and His creation in conveying His religious commands. In His mention that He made the angels messengers without excepting any of them is evidence of the perfection of their obedience to their Lord and their submission to His command, as He, exalted is He, said: {They do not disobey Allah in what He commands them and do what they are commanded}. Since the angels manage, by the permission of Allah, what Allah has entrusted to them, He mentioned their strength for that and the swiftness of their movement, by making them {possessors of wings}, with which they fly, hastening to carry out what they have been commanded: {two, three, or four}; that is, among them is one who has two wings, and one who has three, and one who has four, according to what His wisdom required. {He adds to creation what He wills}; that is, He makes some of His creatures exceed others in the nature of their creation, in strength, in beauty, in the addition of the familiar limbs, and in the beauty of voices and the delight of melodies. {Indeed, Allah is over all things competent}: His power reaches whatever He wills, and nothing is beyond its reach, and among that is the increase of some of His creatures over others.

{2} Then He mentioned His sole administration, giving, and withholding, saying: {Whatever Allah opens to the people of mercy, none can withhold it; and whatever He withholds, none can release it after Him}: this requires attachment to Allah, exalted is He, and need of Him in every respect, and that none be invoked but Him, none be feared but Him, and none be hoped in but Him. {And He is the Exalted in Might}: who has subdued all things. {The Wise}: who places things in their proper places and situates them in their proper stations.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 35, verses 5–7:

{5–6} He, exalted is He, says: ﴿O mankind, indeed the promise of Allah is true﴾ — that is, the resurrection and the recompense for deeds — ﴿is true﴾; meaning there is no doubt about it, no uncertainty, and no hesitation. The textual evidences (al-adillah al-sam'iyyah, the revealed proofs) and the rational proofs (al-baraahin al-'aqliyyah) have indicated this. Since His promise is true, then prepare for it, and hasten to use your noble times for righteous deeds, and let no obstacle cut you off from that. ﴿So let not the worldly life deceive you﴾ — with its pleasures, its desires, and its self-directed aims, so that it distracts you from that for which you were created. ﴿And let not the Deceiver deceive you concerning Allah﴾ — who is Satan, who is in reality your enemy. ﴿So take him as an enemy﴾; that is, let his enmity be ever in your minds, and do not neglect to oppose him at all times, for he sees you while you do not see him, and he is always lying in ambush for you. ﴿He only invites his party that they may be among the companions of the Blaze﴾ — this is his ultimate aim and purpose regarding those who follow him: that they be humiliated to the utmost degree through severe punishment.

{7} Then he mentions that people are divided, according to obedience to Satan or its absence, into two groups, and he mentions the recompense of each of them, saying: ﴿Those who disbelieve﴾; that is, they denied what the messengers brought and what the books indicate. ﴿For them is a severe punishment﴾ — in the Fire of Hell, severe in its essence and its description, and they will abide therein forever. ﴿And those who believe﴾ — in their hearts, in what Allah called them to believe in — ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾ — in accordance with that faith, with their limbs — ﴿for them is forgiveness﴾ — for their sins, by which evil and hardship are removed from them — ﴿and a great reward﴾ — by which the desired goal is attained.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 35, verse 8:

{8} Allah the Exalted says: {Is one whose evil deed has been made attractive to him, so that he sees it as good...} — that is, his evil, ugly deed, which Satan has adorned for him and made appealing in his eyes, {so that he sees it as good}; that is, is he like the one whom Allah has guided to the straight path and the upright religion? Can this one and that one be equal? The first has committed evil and has seen truth as falsehood and falsehood as truth, while the second has done good and has seen truth as truth and falsehood as falsehood. But guidance and misguidance are in the hand of Allah the Exalted. {Indeed, Allah sends astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills, so do not let yourself expire in regret over them} — that is, over the misguided ones whose evil deeds have been made attractive to them and whom Satan has turned away from the truth, {in regret}. So there is no obligation upon you except conveying the message, and you bear no responsibility for their guidance, and Allah is the One who will recompense them for their deeds. {Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do}.

{9} He, may He be exalted, informs of the perfection of His power and the vastness of His generosity, and that He "sends the winds, so they stir up clouds, and We drive them to a dead land," so that He sends down water upon it from them, "and We revive thereby the earth after its death." Thus the lands and the servants come to life, the animals are sustained and graze amid those bounties. "Thus" (kadhalika): the One who revived the earth after its death will raise the dead from their graves after the trial has torn them apart. He will drive rain toward them, just as He drove it toward the dead earth, and send it down upon them, so bodies and spirits come to life from the graves, and they come to stand before Allah, that He may judge among them and separate them by His just judgment.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 35, verse 10:

{10} That is: O you who desire honour! Seek it from the One in whose hand it lies, for honour belongs to Allah, and it is not attained except through obedience to Him. He has mentioned this in His saying: ﴿To Him ascends the good word﴾: such as recitation, glorification (tasbih), praise (tahmid), declaration of His oneness (tahlil), and every good, pure speech. It is raised up to Allah and presented before Him, and Allah praises its speaker among the Exalted Assembly (al-mala' al-a'la). ﴿And righteous deed﴾: from the deeds of the heart and the deeds of the limbs ﴿He raises it﴾: Allah the Exalted raises it to Himself as well, just like the good word. It has also been said: the righteous deed raises the good word, so the raising of the good word corresponds to the righteous deeds of the servant. It is these that lift up his good word, so if he has no righteous deed, no word of his is raised up to Allah the Exalted. These are the deeds that are raised up to Allah the Exalted, and Allah raises their doer and honours him. As for evil deeds, they are the opposite: their doer seeks elevation through them, but he schemes and plots, and that recoils upon him, and he increases only in humiliation and descent. For this reason He said: ﴿And righteous deed raises it, while those who plot evil deeds, for them is a severe punishment﴾: they will be humiliated therein to the utmost degree of humiliation. ﴿And the plotting of those will perish﴾; that is, it will be destroyed and come to nothing, and will benefit them nothing, because it is a plotting for falsehood for the sake of falsehood.

{11} Almighty God mentions the creation of the human being and his transition through these stages, from dust to a drop of semen and what follows. ﴿Then He made you pairs﴾; that is, He has never ceased moving you from stage to stage until He brought you to the point of being pairs: a male who marries a female. By "marriage" is meant offspring and children. Although marriage is among the means toward this, it is coupled with God's decree, His destiny and His knowledge. ﴿No female conceives or gives birth except with His knowledge﴾: likewise, all the stages of the human being are by His knowledge and decree. ﴿Nor is one granted a long life or has any of his life shortened﴾; that is, the one who was granted a long life, ﴿except that it is﴾ by the knowledge of Almighty God. Or: nor is any shortening made of the lifespan of a person who was about to reach it, were it not for the causes of shortened life he pursued, such as fornication, disobedience to parents, severing ties of kinship, and the like, which have been mentioned as causes of a shortened lifespan. The meaning is that the lengthening and shortening of life, whether through a cause or without a cause, are all by the knowledge of Almighty God, and He has recorded that ﴿in a Book﴾, which contains everything that happens to the servant at all his times and throughout the days of his life. ﴿Indeed, that is easy for God﴾; that is, the comprehensiveness of His knowledge of those many known matters, and the comprehensiveness of His Book of them.

These are three of the proofs of the Resurrection and the rising, all of them rational, which God has drawn attention to in these verses: the revival of the earth after its death, and that He who revived it will revive the dead; and the transition of the human being through those stages, so He who brought him into being and moved him stage after stage and state after state until he reached what was decreed for him is more capable of returning him and producing him in the final creation, and that is easier for Him. And the comprehensiveness of His knowledge of all parts of the upper and lower worlds, the minute and the great, that which is in hearts, the fetuses in wombs, the increase and decrease of lifespans, and the recording of all of that in a Book: so He for whom this is easy, His restoring the dead is even easier. Blessed is He whose goodness is abundant, and who has alerted His servants to what is good for them in their livelihood and their final return.

{12} This is a report of His power, wisdom and mercy: that He made the two seas serve the interests of the entire earthly world, and that He did not make them equal. For the public good requires that the rivers be sweet, fresh, with pleasant-tasting water, so that drinkers, planters and cultivators may benefit from them; and that the sea be salty and bitter, lest the air surrounding the earth be corrupted by the stench of the animals that die in the sea. Moreover, it is still and does not flow, so its saltiness protects it from change, and so that its creatures may be better and more delicious. For this reason He said: ﴿And from each of them you eat fresh flesh﴾, meaning from the salt sea and the sweet, ﴿fresh flesh﴾, which is fish whose catch is easy in the sea, ﴿and you extract ornaments to wear﴾, such as pearls, coral and other things found in the sea. These are great benefits for the servants.

Among the benefits and advantages of the sea also is that God subjected it to carry the ships (al-fulk) and vessels, so you see them cutting through and splitting the sea, passing from one region to another and from one place to another, carrying travelers, their loads and their merchandise. Through this a great deal of God's bounty and kindness is attained. For this reason He said: ﴿That you may seek of His bounty, and perhaps you will be grateful﴾.

{13} Among these signs also is God's causing the night to enter into the day and the day into the night: He inserts this into that and that into this; whenever one comes, the other goes; one increases while the other decreases, or they become equal. By this there is accomplished what the interests of the servants require, in their bodies, their animals, their trees and their crops. Likewise, what God placed in the subjugation of the sun and the moon of benefits: light, illumination, movement and rest, the dispersal of the servants in seeking His bounty, and what is in them of ripening fruits and drying what is dried, and other matters that are among the necessities which, if lost, would harm people.

And His saying ﴿each runs for a specified term﴾: meaning, each of the sun and the moon travels in its orbit for as long as God wills them to travel. When the appointed time comes and the end of the world draws near, their motion ceases, their authority is nullified, the moon is eclipsed, the sun is wrapped up, and the stars are scattered.

When God had made clear these great creatures and what is in them of lessons indicating His perfection and kindness, He said: ﴿That is God, your Lord; to Him belongs the dominion﴾: meaning, the One who alone created these things mentioned and subjected them is the Lord, the one worthy of worship, the Deity to whom all dominion belongs. ﴿And those you invoke besides Him﴾: from idols and images, ﴿do not possess﴾ ﴿a speck (qitmir)﴾: meaning, they do not own anything, neither little nor much, not even the qitmir, which is the most insignificant of things. This is from the explicit and general negation; so how can they be invoked when they own nothing of the dominion of the heavens and the earth?!

{14} Despite this: ﴿If you call upon them﴾, they do not hear you, for they are between inanimate objects, the dead and angels occupied with obeying their Lord. ﴿And even if they heard﴾, supposing and assuming it, ﴿they would not respond to you﴾, because they own nothing, and most of them are not pleased with being worshipped by those who worship them. For this reason He said: ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection they will deny your association﴾: meaning, they will disown you, and say: ﴿Exalted are You; You are our Guardian, not them﴾. ﴿And none can inform you like one who is All-Aware﴾: meaning, no one can inform you more truthfully than God, the All-Knowing, the All-Aware. So be certain that this matter which He has reported is as if seen with one's own eyes; do not doubt it or dispute it. These verses thus contain the clear proofs and evidences indicating that He, exalted is He, is the Deity worshipped, who alone deserves no worship but Him, and that worshipping anything other than Him is false, attached to falsehood, and benefits its worshipper nothing.

**Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 35, verses 19–24:**

{19–23} God, exalted is He, informs us that opposites are not equal in God's wisdom or in what He has placed in the natural disposition (fitrah) of His servants. So ﴿the blind man is not equal﴾ to the one who has sight, ﴿nor are the darknesses and the light﴾, ﴿nor the shade and the scorching heat﴾, ﴿nor are the living and the dead alike﴾. Just as it is established among you, beyond any doubt, that these things mentioned are not equal, likewise you should know that the non-equality of opposites in meaning is all the more certain. So the believer and the disbeliever are not equal, nor the guided and the astray, nor the knowledgeable and the ignorant, nor the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire, nor those whose hearts are alive and those whose hearts are dead. Between these things lies a difference and distinction that none knows except God, exalted is He. When you know the ranks, distinguish between things, and it becomes clear what should be competed for in attaining, rather than its opposite, then let the prudent person choose for himself what is more fitting for him and more deserving of preference. ﴿Indeed, God makes hear whom He wills﴾, meaning a hearing of understanding and acceptance, because He, exalted is He, is the Guide who grants success. ﴿And you cannot make hear those who are in the graves﴾; that is, the dead of heart. Or, it means: just as your call benefits none of the dwellers of the graves, likewise it benefits none who turn away and are obstinate. Your duty is only to warn and to convey what you were sent with, whether it is accepted from you or not. For this reason He said: ﴿You are only a warner﴾.

{24} ﴿Indeed, We have sent you with the truth﴾; that is, the mere fact of Our sending you with the truth. God sent you at a time of interval between the messengers, of the effacement of the paths, of the passing away of knowledge, and of a great need for your sending. So God sent you as a mercy to the worlds. Likewise, what We sent you with of the upright religion and the straight path is truth, not falsehood. And likewise what We sent you with of this mighty Qur'an, and what it contains of the wise reminder, is truth and sincerity. ﴿A bringer of good tidings﴾ to whoever obeys you, with God's reward in this world and the next; ﴿and a warner﴾ to whoever disobeys you, with God's punishment in this world and the next. You are not an innovation among the messengers. ﴿There was no nation﴾ among the past nations and bygone generations ﴿but a warner had passed among them﴾, to establish against them the proof of God; ﴿so that whoever perishes might perish by clear evidence, and whoever lives might live by clear evidence﴾.

Allah the Exalted says, challenging the gods of the polytheists and showing their deficiency and the falsehood of their shirk (associating partners with Allah) in every respect:

﴿Say, O Messenger, to them: "Have you considered"; that is, "Tell me about your partners, those you call upon besides Allah"; are they deserving of being called upon and worshipped?! Show me "what they have created of the earth": did they create a sea, or did they create mountains, or did they create an animal, or did they create an inanimate object?! They will acknowledge that the Creator of all things is Allah, the Exalted. Or do your partners have "a share in the heavens": in their creation and their governance?! They will say: "They have no share!" So, if they have created nothing and have not shared with the Creator in His creation, then why have you worshipped them and called upon them while you acknowledge their incapacity?! Thus the rational evidence (al-dalil al-'aqli) for the validity of worshipping them is absent, and this indicates its falsehood.﴾

Then he mentioned the transmitted evidence (al-dalil al-sam'i, i.e., evidence from revelation), and that it too is absent. Therefore He said:

﴿Or have We given them a Book" that speaks by what they used to associate (with Allah)?﴾ — meaning, a book that commands them to associate partners with Allah and to worship idols. "Are they upon clear proof" from that Book revealed to them, in support of the validity of shirk? The matter is not so; for no Book was revealed to them before the Qur'an, and no warner came to them before the Messenger of Allah Muhammad (ﷺ). Even if we assume that a book had been revealed to them and a messenger had been sent to them, and they claimed that it commanded them to their shirk, we would still definitively affirm their lying, because Allah said:

﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me.﴾

So the messengers and the books are all agreed on the command to devote the religion sincerely to Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion, inclining to truth.﴾

If it is said: "If the rational and transmitted evidence has indicated the falsehood of shirk, what then led the polytheists to shirk, when among them are people of intellect, intelligence and perception?" He, the Exalted, answered with His words:

﴿But the wrongdoers promise one another nothing but delusion.﴾ That is: that path upon which they walked has no proof for them; rather, it is only the recommendation of some of them to others, the adornment of some of them for others, the following of the later by the earlier who were astray, and wishes which Satan made them desire, and he made the evil of their deeds appear fair to them. So these took root in their hearts and became one of their qualities, and their removal became difficult and their separation from them became arduous. Thus there resulted what resulted of persistence in disbelief and in false shirk, which is bound to perish.

And that they may know the completeness of His forbearance and forgiveness in granting respite to the sinners and not hastening to punish the disobedient. Yet, if He were to command the sky, it would pelt them [with stones]; and if He were to permit the earth, it would swallow them. But His forgiveness, His forbearance, and His generosity encompass them. "Indeed, He is ever Forbearing, Most Forgiving."

{42} That is: these people who denied you, O Messenger of God, swore an oath with the most emphatic oaths they could muster: {If a warner came to them, they would surely be better guided than any of the (other) nations}; that is, better guided than the Jews and Christians, the People of the Books. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 35, verses 44–45:

{44} The Exalted urges travel through the earth, with both heart and body, for the purpose of taking admonition (i'tibar), not merely for looking and heedlessness, and that they should look at the end of those before them, who denied the messengers. They were greater than these people in wealth, children and strength, and they populated the earth more than these have populated it. When the punishment came upon them, their strength did not avail them, and neither their wealth nor their children availed them anything against God, and the power and will of God took effect upon them. ﴿And God is not to be frustrated by anything in the heavens or on the earth﴾: because of His perfect knowledge and power. ﴿Indeed, He is ever Knowing, Competent﴾.

{45} Then the Exalted mentioned the perfection of His forbearance (hilm), the severity of His respite, and His granting of time to the masters of crimes and sins, and He said: ﴿And if God were to seize mankind for what they have earned﴾: of sins ﴿He would not leave upon it [the earth] any creature moving [on it]﴾; that is, the punishment would have encompassed even the animals that are not charged with responsibility. ﴿But He defers them to a specified term. And when their term comes, indeed God is ever Seeing of His servants﴾: He will recompense them according to what He knows of them of good and evil.

End of the commentary on Surah Fatir. All praise is due to God, Lord of the worlds.

{44} The Exalted urges travel through the earth, with both heart and body, for the purpose of taking admonition (i'tibar), not merely for looking and heedlessness, and that they should look at the end of those before them, who denied the messengers. When the punishment came upon them, their strength did not avail them, and neither their wealth nor their children availed them anything against God, and the power and will of God took effect upon them. ﴿And God is not to be frustrated by anything in the heavens or on the earth﴾: because of His perfect knowledge and power. ﴿Indeed, He is ever Knowing, Competent﴾.

{45} Then the Exalted mentioned the perfection of His forbearance (hilm), the severity of His respite, and His granting of time to the masters of crimes and sins, and He said: ﴿And if God were to seize mankind for what they have earned﴾: of sins ﴿He would not leave upon it [the earth] any creature moving [on it]﴾; that is, the punishment would have encompassed even the animals that are not charged with responsibility. ﴿But He defers them to a specified term. And when their term comes, indeed God is ever Seeing of His servants﴾: He will recompense them according to what He knows of them of good and evil.

End of the commentary on Surah Fatir. All praise is due to God, Lord of the worlds.
